verdict.rationale: Docs show native durability building blocks—sessions auto-persisted to disk, resumable/forkable, a SessionStore adapter to mirror transcripts to custom backends so a session begun on one host can resume on another, and a hosting guide covering session persistence, scaling, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker/K8s—which supports running agents across restarts and redeploys. However, none of the evidence describes a native crash-recovery/checkpointing guarantee mid-task or any integration with dedicated durable-execution frameworks (e.g., Temporal, Restate). missing for 10: explicit mid-execution crash-recovery guarantees, first-party durable-execution framework integrations, independent/hands-on verification of durability claims in production.
